question: Should OpenClaw adopt `queryInstructionTemplate` as a durable memory config and public plugin/provider contract for model-specific query formatting?
rationale: The implementation is additive and defaults off, but it creates a new user setting, four provider contract additions, and an SDK helper that require long-term compatibility ownership.

options.title: Adopt The Opt-In Contract
options.body: Accept the shared helper and boolean setting after the review findings, current-head proof, and merge conflicts are addressed.

options.title: Keep It Provider-Local
options.body: Limit template policy to the OpenAI-compatible owner surfaces without promoting the broader plugin/provider option.

options.title: Pause For General Design
options.body: Hold or close the PR until maintainers define a more general asymmetric embedding prompt contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt The Opt-In Contract
recommendation.body: Accept the shared helper and boolean setting after the review findings, current-head proof, and merge conflicts are addressed.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged feature history connects this person most directly to the memory embedding and provider boundary being expanded.
